arxiv-2407-02258.title: SiamTST: A Novel Representation Learning Framework for Enhanced Multivariate Time Series Forecasting applied to Telco Networks
arxiv-2407-02258.creator: Simen Kristoffersen, Peter Skaar Nordby, Sara Malacarne, Massimiliano Ruocco, Pablo Ortiz
arxiv-2407-02258.description: Abstract We introduce SiamTST , a novel representation learning framework for multivariate time series. SiamTST integrates a Siamese network with attention, channel-independent patching, and normalization techniques to achieve superior performance. Evaluated on a real-world industrial telecommunication dataset, SiamTST demonstrates significant improvements in forecasting accuracy over existing methods.

arxiv-2502-09310.title: Global Stabilization of Chemostats with Nonzero Mortality and Substrate Dynamics
arxiv-2502-09310.creator: Iasson Karafyllis, Epiphane Loko, Miroslav Krstić, Antoine Chaillet
arxiv-2502-09310.description: Abstract Abstract: In “chemostat”-type population models that incorporate substrate (nutrient) dynamics, the dependence of the birth (or growth) rate on the substrate concentration introduces nonlinear coupling that creates a challenge for stabilization that is global, namely, for all positive concentrations of the biomass and nutrients.

arxiv-2507-03270.title: Soft breaking of translational symmetry in the ϕ 4 \phi^{4} theory
arxiv-2507-03270.creator: F. C. E. Lima, C. A. S. Almeida
arxiv-2507-03270.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by F. C. E. Lima, C. A. S. Almeida. Abstract: We consider a two-dimensional scalar field theory that modifies the standard ϕ 4 \phi^{4} model by introducing a smooth breaking of translational invariance through a hyperbolic generalizing function. This function explicitly breaks the ℤ 2 \mathds{Z}_{2} symmetry; however, it also introduces a mechanism capable of generating new energy minima (vacua) and of localizing or delocalizing field fluctuations around these vacua. Thus, this mechanism enables a continuous transformation of kink/antikink-like structures into compacted asymmetric double-kink/antikink.

arxiv-2508-20216.title: Reverse Designing Ferroelectric Capacitors with Machine Learning-based Compact Modeling
arxiv-2508-20216.creator: Diego Ferrer, Jack Hutchins, Revanth Koduru, Sumeet Kumar Gupta, Admedullah Aziz
arxiv-2508-20216.description: Abstract Machine learning-based compact models provide a rapid and efficient approach for estimating device behavior across multiple input parameter variations. In this study, we introduce two reverse-design algorithms that utilize these compact models to identify device parameters corresponding to desired electrical characteristics. The algorithms effectively determine parameter sets, such as layer thicknesses, required to achieve specific device performance criteria.

arxiv-2602-07377.title: Inference under First-Order Degeneracy Thanks: Emails: xinyue.bei@austin.utexas.edu and mnavjeevan@tamu.edu . We thank Zheng Fang, Matt Masten, Andres Santos, and seminar participants at the UT Austin Econometrics Writing Seminar for their helpful comments. Mengyuan Jiang provided excellent research
arxiv-2602-07377.creator: Xinyue Bei, Manu Navjeevan
arxiv-2602-07377.description: Abstract We study inference in models where a transformation of parameters exhibits first-order degeneracy — that is, its gradient is zero or close to zero, making the standard delta method invalid. A leading example is causal mediation analysis, where the indirect effect is a product of coefficients and the gradient degenerates near the origin.

openalex-w2011607584.title: A bitter cup: climate change profile of global production of Arabica and Robusta coffee

pmc-10599027.title: Hypovitaminosis D in persons with Down syndrome and autism spectrum disorder
pmc-10599027.creator: Natalie K. Boyd, Julia Nguyen, Mellad M. Khoshnood, Timothy Jiang, Lina Nguyen, Lorena Mendez, Noemi A. Spinazzi, Melanie A. Manning, Michael S. Rafii, Jonathan D. Santoro
pmc-10599027.description: BackgroundPlasma levels of vitamin D have been reported to be low in persons with Down syndrome (DS) and existing data is limited to small and homogenous cohorts. This is of particular importance in persons with DS given the high rates of autoimmune disease in this population and the known relationship between vitamin D and immune function.

pmc-10649320.title: LSTM4piRNA: Efficient piRNA Detection in Large-Scale Genome Databases Using a Deep Learning-Based LSTM Network
pmc-10649320.creator: Chun-Chi Chen, Yi-Ming Chan, Hyundoo Jeong, Peter Hamar, Alexander Tonevitsky
pmc-10649320.description: Piwi-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a new class of small, non-coding RNAs, crucial in the regulation of gene expression. Recent research has revealed links between piRNAs, viral defense mechanisms, and certain human cancers. Due to their clinical potential, there is a great interest in identifying piRNAs from large genome databases through efficient computational methods.

pmc-11393189.title: Anti-MDA5 autoantibodies predict clinical dynamics of dermatomyositis following SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination: a retrospective statistical analysis of case reports
pmc-11393189.creator: Christian R Klein, Annkristin Heine, Peter Brossart, Pantelis Karakostas, Valentin Sebastian Schäfer
pmc-11393189.description: Since the introduction of mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2, the induction of autoimmunity by mRNA vaccination has been discussed. Several cases of dermatomyositis (DM) associated with mRNA vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 infection have been reported. The question is whether there is a common pathomechanism for the induction of DM by this mRNA vaccination.

pmc-11548442.description: To address the issues of target feature blurring and increased false detections caused by high compression rates in deepfake videos, as well as the high computational resource requirements of existing face extractors, we propose a lightweight face extractor to assist deepfake detection, GCS-YOLOv8.

pmc-11643752.title: Efficient and Stable Deep-Blue 0D Copper-Based Halide TEA2Cu2I4 with Near-Unity Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Light-Emitting Diodes
pmc-11643752.creator: Fang Yuan, Xiaoyun Liu, Songting Zhang, Peichao Zhu, Fawad Ali, Chenjing Zhao, Shuaiqi He, Qianhao Ma, Jingrui Li, Kunping Guo, Lu Li, Zhaoxin Wu
pmc-11643752.description: Achieving deep-blue light with high color saturation remains a critical challenge in the development of white light-emitting diode (LED) technology, necessitating luminescent materials that excel in efficiency, low toxicity, and stability. Here, we report the synthesis of [N(C2H5)4]2Cu2I4 (TEA2Cu2I4) single crystals (SCs), which exhibit deep-blue photoluminescence (PL) at 450 nm.

pmc-12400860.title: Association of obesity-related anthropometric indicators with chronic constipation and diarrhea among U.S. adults: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12400860.creator: Yu Ning, Xiaoting Hu, Laifu Li, Yan Zhuang, Fei Dai
pmc-12400860.description: AimPrior studies have linked obesity indicators to constipation/diarrhea, but multi-measure comparisons remain limited. We analyzed these associations in U.S. adults.MethodsThis cross-sectional study utilized data from three cycles (2005–2010) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). The final analysis included 13,105 participants after excluding those aged < 20 years or with missing data for any study variables.

pmc-12429137.title: Norepinephrine Onset Time and Mortality in Patients with Septic Shock Treated in the Emergency Department
pmc-12429137.creator: German Devia Jaramillo, Jose Wdroo Motta Hernández, William Gerardo Donoso Zapata, Ecaterina Scarlatescu
pmc-12429137.description: Introduction: Sepsis, and particularly septic shock, is a life-threatening condition associated with high mortality rates in the emergency department. Timely interventions can significantly reduce these unacceptably high mortality rates. While some studies have demonstrated reduced mortality with early norepinephrine initiation, there is limited research on this intervention specifically within the emergency department setting.

pmc-12935979.title: Research on grape leaf disease recognition method based on improved YOLOv8n model
pmc-12935979.creator: Huiping Guo, Jiarui Cao, Yi Wang, Linrui Rong, Fuzeng Yang, Liangliang Zhu, Weiguo Zhang
pmc-12935979.description: Grape leaf disease recognition models face challenges such as large model sizes and a lack of classification for various disease types. This study proposes an enhanced grape leaf disease recognition model using an improved version of YOLOv8n, addressing these limitations. To improve performance, several modifications were made to the original YOLOv8n architecture.

pmc-13242494.title: The argument-based approach to validity: theory, assumptions, evidence, and consequences
pmc-13242494.creator: Melanie Hawkins, Richard Sawatzky, Kevin Weinfurt, Sharla Cartner, Scott Gill, Richard Osborne, Nancy Mayo, Kara Schick-Makaroff, Mirjam Sprangers, R J Wirth, Gerald R Elsworth, Sandra Nolte
pmc-13242494.description: BackgroundConcerns about measurement validation are often expressed as imperatives to use a “valid measure”. However, validity is not a characteristic of a measure. Instead, validation and validity refer to score interpretation within a context of use. This is important because responses to health measures can be different in different contexts, influencing equitable consequences of measurement.

pmc-13441444.title: Comparison of clinical and histopathological features between serum IgG4-negative and serum IgG4-positive patients with type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis: A single-center, retrospective study
pmc-13441444.creator: Xiaorong Tian, Dongling Wan, Hanbin Zhu, Wanshun Li, Yuyan Zhou, Hanxiao Cui, Jiaheng Xu, Zhenghui Yang, Jiayu Li, Deyu Zhang, Liqi Sun, Zhendong Jin, Haojie Huang
pmc-13441444.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objective:In type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP), serum immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4) has a complex correlation with pathology. In this study, clinical/histopathological traits of serum IgG4-negative/positive (N/P) patients were compared, and serum IgG4-tissue IgG4 correlations were explored to aid accurate diagnosis/typing.Material and Methods:A retrospective analysis was performed on 78 type 1 AIP patients (screened from 160 eligible cases through inclusion/exclusion criteria, International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria-confirmed at Changhai Hospital (December 2019-2023).

pmc-13675236.title: Formation of hydroxyapatite on tooth surfaces by calcium hypophosphite in saliva
pmc-13675236.creator: Pascal Fandrich, Erik Schulze zur Wiesche, Bennett Tochukwu Amaechi, Joachim Enax
pmc-13675236.description: AimThis in vitro study aimed to investigate whether calcium hypophosphite (CaP) mediates hydroxyapatite (HAP) formation in artificial and human saliva and, in a proof-of-principle toothbrushing model, promotes mineral deposition and occlusion of dentinal tubules.MethodsA CaP solution was added to artificial saliva and human saliva, respectively. The resulting precipitate was analyzed using X-ray powder diffraction (XRD).
